name: Desktop 98
fit: Dev portfolios, nostalgic products, games, interactive CVs
keywords: windows 98 os nostalgia pixel retro desktop beige
idea: The site is a beige-box operating system. Sections are windows you drag, focus and close; projects live in folders; a taskbar and Start menu are the navigation.
note: Live: drag windows by their title bars, click to focus, close with ×. Click a desktop icon twice to open it, or use the Start menu. The installer loops.
borrowed: Late-90s desktop operating systems: the teal desktop, 3D-bevelled grey chrome, navy gradient title bars, pixel UI type, setup wizards with block progress bars, a Start menu with a vertical brand band, and the taskbar clock.
mood: Nostalgic, tactile, explorable. Suits developer portfolios, retro-tech products, games, and interactive CVs where poking around is the experience. Works best when every window holds real content, not gimmicks.

type.meta: UI · Pixelify Sans 400 at 14–16px; no other family

motion: No easing anywhere: windows snap, menus pop, progress jumps a block at a time.
Drag via pointer capture on the title bar, clamped to the desktop; focus raises `z-index` and greys every other title bar.
Pressed state = inverted bevel (swap the light and dark border colours).
watchouts: Desktop metaphors collapse on phones. Stack windows as full-width cards below ~700px.
Every window must be reachable without dragging or double-clicking (Start menu, taskbar, keyboard).
Pastiche, not a clone: don't copy a real OS's logo, sounds or names.
